claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The alloy has a lamellar two-phase microstructure.
The two phases are a soft FCC phase and a hard Al-Ni-rich B2 phase.
The FCC phase is more corrosion resistant than the B2 phase.
The B2 phase is susceptible to localized corrosion and pitting in chloride-containing sulfuric acid.
The passive film on AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is stable at low temperature and unstable at high temperature in chloride-containing sulfuric acid.
Room temperature and above define the temperature range in which the passive film is unstable.
The thermally unstable passive film is located especially on the B2 phase.
Mechanical wear locally removes the unstable passive film.
Removal of the passive film exposes fresh reactive surface and accelerates localized corrosion.
At room temperature and above, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 undergoes both pitting and dissolution in the acid solution.
Pitting and selective dissolution locally weaken the surface.
Corrosion-induced local weakening increases subsequent wear damage.
Repeated film removal and localized corrosion create a positive feedback loop between wear and corrosion.
Total degradation during simultaneous wear and corrosion exceeds the arithmetic sum of degradation measured in separate wear and corrosion tests.
Coupled exposure increases wear-track depth and volume loss relative to isolated wear.
Coupled exposure increases pit density and pit depth relative to corrosion without mechanical disturbance.
The proposed synergistic effect occurs only when passive-film-destabilizing temperature and active mechanical wear are simultaneously present.
Below the passive-film instability threshold, the coupled degradation effect does not occur.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for separate tests under matching temperatures and environments, but the isolated-wear baseline is specified as dry, inert, or non-corrosive rather than environmentally matched to the chloride-containing acid used in the coupled test.
